chunks: Tamim ibn Abd Allah ibn Tamim al-Qurashi (mercy of Allah be upon him) said: My father narrated to me, from Hamdan ibn Sulayman al-Naysaburi, from Ali ibn Muhammad ibn al-Jahm, who said: I attended the assembly of al-Ma'mun, and with him was al-Rida, Ali ibn Musa (peace be upon them both).

Al-Ma'mun asked him: 'O son of the Messenger of Allah, is it not from your saying that the Prophets are infallible?' He replied: 'Yes.' He asked him about some verses from the Quran, and among what he asked was: 'Then inform me about the saying of Ibrahim: My Lord, show me how You give life to the dead. He said: What! And do you not believe? He said: Yes, but that my heart may be at ease.'

Al-Rida (peace be upon him) replied: Indeed, Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, revealed to Ibrahim (peace be upon him) that I will choose a friend for Me from among My servants; if he asks Me for the revival of the dead, I will answer him. It occurred to Ibrahim (peace be upon him) that he was that friend, so he said: 'My Lord, show me how You give life to the dead.' He said: 'What! And do you not believe?' He said: 'Yes, but that my heart may be at ease regarding the friendship.'
He said: 'Then take four of the birds, then train them to follow you, then place on every mountain a part of them, then call them, they will come to you flying; and know that Allah is Mighty, Wise.'

Then Ibrahim (peace be upon him) took an eagle, a duck, a peacock, and a rooster, and chopped them into small pieces. Then he placed a part of them on each of the ten mountains that were around him. He placed their beaks between his fingers, then called them by their names, and placed seeds and water near him. Those parts flew from one to another until the bodies were complete. Each body came and joined its neck and head. Ibrahim released their beaks, and they flew. Then they stood, drank from that water, and ate from that seed, and said: 'O Prophet of Allah, you have given us life; may Allah give you life.' Ibrahim (peace be upon him) said: 'It is Allah who gives life and causes death, and He is Powerful over all things.'
Al-Ma'mun said: 'May Allah bless you, O Abu al-Hasan.' The tradition is long; we have taken from it what was needed.

key_terms.لِيَطْمَئِنَّ قَلْبِي: That my heart may be at ease (seeking certainty)
key_terms.يُحْيِي وَيُمِيتُ: He gives life and causes death

ai.seo_question: How did Imam al-Rida explain the verse 'Show me how You give life to the dead' in relation to Prophet Ibrahim's faith?
ai.summary: In this narrative from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Tawhid*, Imam Ali al-Rida (AS) engages Caliph al-Ma'mun to clarify the nature of Prophetic infallibility, specifically addressing the apparent doubt in Prophet Ibrahim’s (AS) request 'How will You give life to the dead?' The Imam elucidates that Ibrahim’s query was not for confirmation of faith but for *itmi'nan* (deep, experiential certainty) regarding his status as *Khalilullah* (Friend of God), thereby distinguishing between the certainty of belief and the certainty of divine promise. This incident underscores the Shia theological view that Prophets, while infallible, may seek heightened spiritual assurance to strengthen their connection with the Divine.
